newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma to meet Belarussian leader.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma to meet Belarussian leader.

text.p: Ukraine's security chief said on Wednesday Kiev was reserving judgement over plans for a merger between Russia and Belarus and announced President Leonid Kuchma would meet Belarussian leader Alexander Lukashenko this week.

"This is up to Russia and Belarus. We are not very concerned but our reaction will come later," Volodymyr Horbulin, head of the powerful Security Council, told a news briefing. "This is a step to put pressure on NATO's plans to enlarge."
Russian President Boris Yeltsin, in hospital suffering from pneumonia, sent a letter to Lukashenko on Monday calling for a referendum on joining the two Slav states.
Senior Russian officials have said a merger, long advocated by Lukashenko, would be the best answer to NATO's planned enlargement, due to be announced later this year.

Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic are leading candidates for initial admission. Both Russia and Belarus, under Lukashenko's hardline rule, oppose expansion, but Ukraine says it has no objections.
Horbulin said Kuchma and Lukashenko would meet on Friday in the Belarussian city of Gomel, just over the border, at a jointly owned plant producing combine harvesters.
Sources in Kuchma's administration said they wanted more details of the proposed merger.
"We just want to ask -- what is going to happen to Belarus itself?" one source said. "Will it remain an independent state?"
Relations between Ukraine and Belarus have worsened since Kuchma turned down Lukashenko's proposal for a meeting on the eve of his November referendum which broadly extended his powers.
Ukraine was among countries in the region which expressed concern at the referendum, denounced as unfair and undemocratic by the Council of Europe and other Western organisations.
Last week Lukashenko, in response to Moscow's accusations that Russia was inundated with cheap Belarussian and Ukrainian vodka, threatened to close the border with Ukraine.
